judged_text: The guests array has no maximum length (z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max()), so a single mutation can create an unbounded number of attendee rows and trigger an unbounded email fan-out. One authenticated request with thousands of emails inserts thousands of attendee rows and fans out thousands of outbound emails plus a calendar update in a single synchronous request path — unbounded storage growth and request amplification on the user-facing mutation path, with no cap anywhere in the handler either.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` cap. The handler `addGuestsHandler` (`addGuests.handler.ts`) then `createMany` inserts one attendee row per entry in `uniqueGuests` and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which constructs a `Promise` per attendee (and additional organizer/team-member emails) in `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`packages/emails/email-manager.ts`) and awaits `Promise.all`. This makes the user-facing mutation path susceptible to unbounded row creation and email fan-out (plus `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`) in a single request, enabling request amplification/abuse and unbounded storage growth.
